MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the next number in the pattern 11, 14, 17, 20, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 26
   B. 23
   C. 24
   D. 22

2. Which is the largest number: 742, 724, 472, 427? (1 mark)
   A. 472
   B. 724
   C. 427
   D. 742

3. Which of these is a multiple of 7? (1 mark)
   A. 44
   B. 41
   C. 43
   D. 42

4. In the number 91,724, the digit 9 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Ones
   B. Tens
   C. Ten thousands
   D. Hundreds

5. What number is the Roman numeral V? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 4
   C. 6
   D. 7

6. Which sum checks that 8,500 − 3,275 = 5,225? (1 mark)
   A. 5,225 − 3,275
   B. 8,500 + 3,275
   C. 5,225 + 3,275
   D. 8,500 + 5,225

7. When we subtract 1,236 from 4,000, what do we do first? (1 mark)
   A. Take the smaller digit from the bigger digit in each column
   B. Regroup from the thousands because there are zeros in the tens and hundreds
   C. Subtract the thousands digits only
   D. Add 1,236 to 4,000

8. Estimate 9,317 − 4,582 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 4,740
   B. 4,840
   C. 4,730
   D. 4,750

9. Estimate 27 × 13 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 3,000
   B. 400
   C. 300
   D. 200

10. What is 34 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 340
   B. 34,000
   C. 134
   D. 3,400

11. What is 7 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 7,000
   B. 107
   C. 70
   D. 700

12. What is 72 ÷ 3? (1 mark)
   A. 25
   B. 23
   C. 24
   D. 34

13. A circle is cut into 8 equal parts and 3 parts are shaded. What fraction is not shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 3/8
   B. 5/8
   C. 5/3
   D. 8/5

14. What is 3/8 of 40? (1 mark)
   A. 25
   B. 20
   C. 5
   D. 15

15. How many hundredths make one tenth? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 100
   C. 1
   D. 10

16. What is the total value of the digit 7 in 9.27? (1 mark)
   A. 0.007
   B. 0.07
   C. 7
   D. 0.7

17. Which is greater, 0.5 or 0.45? (1 mark)
   A. They are equal
   B. 0.5
   C. 0.45
   D. It cannot be told

18. Which expression shows "twice a number p"? (1 mark)
   A. p − 2
   B. p + 2
   C. p ÷ 2
   D. 2p

19. Which expression shows "a number y shared equally among 4 people"? (1 mark)
   A. y + 4
   B. 4y
   C. y ÷ 4
   D. y − 4

20. A pencil starts at the 0 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 7 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 8 cm
   B. 6 cm
   C. 9 cm
   D. 7 cm

21. What is the perimeter of a shape? (1 mark)
   A. Its longest side
   B. The space inside it
   C. The number of its corners
   D. The distance all the way round its edge

22. A fence uses 3 pieces of wire, each 1 m 25 cm long. What is the total length of wire? (1 mark)
   A. 1 m 28 cm
   B. 3 m 65 cm
   C. 4 m 75 cm
   D. 3 m 75 cm

23. Which shape has the same number of rows and columns of unit squares? (1 mark)
   A. A circle
   B. A square
   C. A rectangle that is not a square
   D. A triangle

24. A square is covered with 8 rows of 8 unit squares. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 64 square units
   B. 32 square units
   C. 16 square units
   D. 72 square units

25. A cuboid is 4 blocks long, 3 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 28 blocks
   B. 9 blocks
   C. 24 blocks
   D. 12 blocks

26. One layer of a cuboid has 9 blocks and there are 6 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 48 blocks
   B. 15 blocks
   C. 63 blocks
   D. 54 blocks

27. Two quarters of a litre are the same as (1 mark)
   A. 1/2 L
   B. 1/4 L
   C. 3/4 L
   D. 1 L

28. A shopper buys 3/4 kg of tomatoes and 1/2 kg of onions. What is the total mass? (1 mark)
   A. 1 1/2 kg
   B. 1 kg
   C. 5/8 kg
   D. 1 1/4 kg

29. What is 5 1/2 kg + 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 6 1/2 kg
   B. 5 3/4 kg
   C. 6 1/4 kg
   D. 6 kg

30. When is a shadow shortest? (1 mark)
   A. Around midday
   B. Early in the morning
   C. Late in the afternoon
   D. At night

31. What is 3 h 50 min + 2 h 25 min? (1 mark)
   A. 6 h 25 min
   B. 6 h 5 min
   C. 5 h 15 min
   D. 6 h 15 min

32. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 11 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 1. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 12:05
   B. 11:05
   C. 11:55
   D. 11:01

33. How long is a lesson that starts at 10:30 a.m. and ends at 2:15 p.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 4 h 45 min
   B. 3 h 30 min
   C. 3 h 45 min
   D. 3 h 55 min

34. A customer pays with Ksh 2,000 for goods that cost Ksh 1,340. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 760
   B. Ksh 3,340
   C. Ksh 660
   D. Ksh 650

35. How many cents are in Ksh 8? (1 mark)
   A. 8,000 cents
   B. 800 cents
   C. 108 cents
   D. 80 cents

36. Which is the same as half a shilling? (1 mark)
   A. 5 cents
   B. 50 cents
   C. 10 cents
   D. 500 cents

37. Kip faces South and makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. North
   C. West
   D. East

38. The table shows the vehicles that passed a school gate (10 vehicles): matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1. How many more are there of matatu than of boda boda? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 3
   C. 5
   D. 7

39. In a table, a row goes (1 mark)
   A. round in a circle
   B. across the page
   C. down the page
   D. diagonally only

40. In a tally chart, 2 groups of five and 4 more single tally marks are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 13
   B. 14
   C. 15
   D. 19

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. What number must be added to 3,425 to make 5,743? Explain how you found it. (3 marks)

42. Explain why multiplying by 100 puts two zeros on the end of a whole number. (3 marks)

43. Mama Njoki has 24 oranges. She gives 3/8 of them to her neighbours and 1/4 of them to a friend. (a) How many oranges does she give to her neighbours? (b) How many does she give to her friend? (c) How many oranges are left? (5 marks)

44. Amina faces south. She makes a quarter turn anticlockwise, then a half turn, then a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does she face at the end? Show each step. (5 marks)

45. Mama Kioko sells 3 bags of mangoes (m) and 2 bags of oranges (o) on Monday, then 1 bag of mangoes and 4 bags of oranges on Tuesday. Write an expression and simplify it. (4 marks)

46. A trader has 12 kg of beans and 8 kg of maize. He sells 5 kg of the beans. Find the total mass of the beans and maize he has left. (3 marks)

47. Explain why we add the numbers in the total row of a table. (3 marks)

48. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. Draw it roughly, label the sides and find its perimeter. (3 marks)

49. Divide 58 by 4 and give the remainder. (3 marks)

50. Divide 91 by 7 and check by multiplication. (3 marks)

51. Tabitha cuts a 7 m 20 cm rope into 6 pieces of equal length. Find the length of one piece. (3 marks)

52. A matatu carries m passengers. At a stop 8 get in and 3 get out. Write and simplify an expression for the number of passengers now. (3 marks)

53. Write the first five multiples of 9. (2 marks)

54. A farmer has 95 eggs to pack into trays that each hold 6 eggs. (a) How many full trays are there and how many eggs are left over? (b) How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (5 marks)

55. Give two differences between perimeter and area. (3 marks)

56. The raw data for 10 pupils' favourite fruits is: mango, banana, mango, orange, banana, mango, pawpaw, mango, banana, orange. Make a tally table for this data. (4 marks)

57. A class has 30 pupils. Two fifths of them walk to school. How many pupils walk to school? (3 marks)

58. Njeri had Ksh 5,000. She bought a school bag for Ksh 1,850. How much change did she get? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — 23
   The rule is add 3. 20 + 3 = 23.

2. D — 742
   Compare the digits from the left. The largest number is 742.

3. D — 42
   42 = 7 × 6, so 42 is a multiple of 7.

4. C — Ten thousands
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 9 is in the ten thousands place.

5. A — 5
   V stands for 5.

6. C — 5,225 + 3,275
   Addition undoes subtraction. 5,225 + 3,275 = 8,500, the starting number.

7. B — Regroup from the thousands because there are zeros in the tens and hundreds
   The ones digit 0 is smaller than 6 and the tens and hundreds are zeros, so we borrow from the thousands.

8. A — 4,740
   9,317 rounds to 9,320 and 4,582 rounds to 4,580. 9,320 − 4,580 = 4,740.

9. C — 300
   27 rounds to 30 and 13 rounds to 10. 30 × 10 = 300.

10. D — 3,400
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 34 × 100 = 3,400.

11. D — 700
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 7 × 100 = 700.

12. C — 24
   3 × 24 = 72, so 72 ÷ 3 = 24.

13. B — 5/8
   Not shaded: 8 − 3 = 5 parts, so 5/8.

14. D — 15
   40 ÷ 8 = 5 and 5 × 3 = 15. So 3/8 of 40 is 15.

15. D — 10
   One tenth is 10/100, so 10 hundredths make 1 tenth.

16. B — 0.07
   The digit 7 is in the hundredths place, so its total value is 0.07.

17. B — 0.5
   Compare the tenths first. 0.5 is greater than 0.45.

18. D — 2p
   The key words tell us the operation. "twice a number p" is written 2p.

19. C — y ÷ 4
   The key words tell us the operation. "a number y shared equally among 4 people" is written y ÷ 4.

20. D — 7 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 7 − 0 = 7 cm.

21. D — The distance all the way round its edge
   Perimeter is the total length of all the sides.

22. D — 3 m 75 cm
   125 × 3 = 375 cm = 3 m 75 cm.

23. B — A square
   A square has equal sides, so its number of rows equals its number of columns.

24. A — 64 square units
   Area = 8 × 8 = 64 square units.

25. C — 24 blocks
   One layer has 4 × 3 = 12 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 12 × 2 = 24 blocks.

26. D — 54 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 9 × 6 = 54 blocks.

27. A — 1/2 L
   1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2.

28. D — 1 1/4 kg
   3/4 + 2/4 = 5/4 = 1 1/4 kg.

29. D — 6 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 5 1/2 kg + 1/2 kg = 6 kg.

30. A — Around midday
   At midday the Sun is highest, so shadows are very short.

31. D — 6 h 15 min
   Add the minutes and hours, then change 60 minutes into 1 hour. The answer is 6 h 15 min.

32. B — 11:05
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 1 shows 1 × 5 = 5 minutes, so the time is 11:05.

33. C — 3 h 45 min
   Count on from 10:30 a.m. to 2:15 p.m.. The total is 3 h 45 min.

34. C — Ksh 660
   Change = amount paid − cost = 2,000 − 1,340 = Ksh 660.

35. B — 800 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 8 = 8 × 100 = 800 cents.

36. B — 50 cents
   One shilling is 100 cents, so half a shilling is 50 cents.

37. D — East
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. South followed by a quarter turn anticlockwise gives East.

38. B — 3
   5 − 2 = 3.

39. B — across the page
   Rows go across and columns go down.

40. B — 14
   2 × 5 + 4 = 14.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2,318. Subtract 5,743 − 3,425 = 2,318.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using subtraction, 1 mark for the working, 1 mark for the answer 2,318.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each digit moves two places to the left, so it becomes 100 times bigger. The empty tens and ones places are filled with zeros.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for digits moving two places, 1 mark for 100 times bigger, 1 mark for zeros filling places.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 9 oranges (b) 6 oranges (c) 9 oranges
   Working / marking points: (a) 24 ÷ 8 = 3, 3 × 3 = 9 (2 marks); (b) 24 ÷ 4 = 6 (1 mark); (c) 24 − 9 − 6 = 9 (2 marks).

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: North
   Working / marking points: South then a quarter turn anticlockwise gives east (2 marks). East then a half turn gives west (1 mark). West then a quarter turn clockwise gives north (1 mark). Final answer north (1 mark).

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3m + 2o + m + 4o = 4m + 6o
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the expression, 1 mark for 4m, 1 mark for 6o, 1 mark for the final answer.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: 15 kg
   Working / marking points: 12 − 5 = 7 kg of beans (1 mark); 7 + 8 (1 mark); 15 kg (1 mark).

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: To check that we have counted everything and that the total equals the number of items collected. If it is different we must count again.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for checking, 1 mark for comparing with the number collected, 1 mark for counting again.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Perimeter = 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a labelled rectangle, 1 mark for adding all four sides, 1 mark for 26 cm.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: 14 remainder 2
   Working / marking points: 5 tens ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 1 (1 mark); 18 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 2 (1 mark); answer 14 R 2 (1 mark).

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: 13. Check: 13 × 7 = 91.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7 × 13, 1 mark for 13, 1 mark for the check.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 m 20 cm
   Working / marking points: 720 ÷ 6 = 120 cm (2 marks); 120 cm = 1 m 20 cm (1 mark).

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: m + 8 − 3 = m + 5
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for m + 8, 1 mark for taking away 3, 1 mark for simplifying to m + 5.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first three and 1 mark for the last two.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 15 full trays and 5 eggs left over (b) 16 trays
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 95 ÷ 6 = 15 remainder 5, 1 mark for stating both, 1 mark for the leftover eggs needing another tray, 1 mark for 16.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Perimeter is the distance round the edge and is measured in units of length such as cm. Area is the flat surface inside the shape and is measured in square units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning of each and 1 mark for the units.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mango 4 (||||), banana 3 (|||), orange 2 (||), pawpaw 1 (|); total 10.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct count of two fruits (2 marks), 1 mark for correct tally marks, 1 mark for the total 10.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: 12 pupils
   Working / marking points: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 (1 mark); 6 × 2 = 12 (1 mark); answer with unit (1 mark).

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 3,150
   Working / marking points: 5,000 − 1,850 = 3,150. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the answer with Ksh.
